category_title: Third-grade African American students who rely on picture support and skip text when overwhelmed
minimal_context: Tommy is reading a text with high word density and illustrations aloud during a tutoring session.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please read this page out loud for me.

STUDENT: (Looks at the page) That's a lot of words. I'm just going to skip down to this line here.

TUTOR: Okay, go ahead and read that part.

STUDENT: Pulled on his, pulled on his shirt and put.

TUTOR: Look at the words again. Are you sure it says shirt?

STUDENT: (Points confidently to the illustration on the page) Yeah, shirt. You see his shirt?

options.A: Play the student's recorded reading and pause at preselected miscues to have him listen back to the recording.
options.B: Provide individual storage space for the student, such as a chair bag or a desk with compartments.
options.C: Place an exclusive display board in the tutoring space only for the student to display his work.
options.D: Adjust seating arrangements to place the student closer to the tutor, next to a peer, or near the board.
